lessons.title: Why groundnut samples must be representative
lessons.html:
Why groundnut samples must be representative

Groundnuts (peanuts) come to the depot from the farm, in their shells (unshelled) or as kernels (shelled), in bags or in bulk. The grader tests a sample to decide the grade. The farmer is paid on that grade, and the buyer gets what the grade says.

A representative sample is a small part that is the same as the whole delivery. It has the same amount of good nuts, damaged nuts, loose shells, sand, stones and moisture as the whole load.

Why groundnuts need extra care

  • Groundnuts grow under the ground, so loads often have sand, soil and stones. These sink to the bottom of bags and loads.
  • Damaged or mouldy groundnuts can carry aflatoxin, a poison made by a mould. It is dangerous to people and animals even in small amounts. A good sample helps the grader find mouldy nuts.
  • Kernels, shells, broken pieces and dust separate when the load is shaken on the road. Light shells move to the top, heavy sand moves down.

Example

A farmer delivers 200 bags of unshelled groundnuts. If the sampler only takes nuts from the top of five bags near the door, the sample may look clean. But many bags at the back may have more sand and mouldy pods. The grade on paper is then wrong.

Tools

  • Bag sampling probe for bags.
  • Bulk probe for trucks and trailers.
  • Clean sample container or bag.
  • Sample divider.
  • Labels and seals.

All tools must be clean and dry. Old nuts or dust left in a probe will go into the next sample and give the wrong result.

lessons.title: Taking, mixing and labelling the groundnut sample
lessons.html:
Taking the sample

Bagged groundnuts

  1. Take samples from bags spread over the whole stack or load: top, middle, bottom, front and back. Take the number of bags your depot procedure says.
  2. Push the bag probe in at an angle from one corner towards the middle so it reaches deep into the bag.
  3. Pull it out and empty it into the sample container.
  4. For unshelled nuts, some depots open a bag and take nuts by hand from top to bottom, because pods can jam a probe. Follow your procedure.

Bulk groundnuts

  1. Engine off and handbrake on before you go near the truck.
  2. Use the platform with rails.
  3. Probe at the points your procedure shows, spread over the load, all the way to the bottom.

Mixing and dividing

  • Pour the whole sample through the sample divider. Keep dividing until you have the size the grader needs.
  • Include everything: sand, stones, shells and loose kernels. Do not throw anything out, because the grader must measure it.
  • Never pick out the good or bad nuts.

Labelling

  • Put the sample in a clean bag or container.
  • Write: producer name or number, truck registration, delivery or ticket number, date, number of bags, and shelled or unshelled.
  • Seal the sample and take it to the grading room straight away.
  • Keep the retained sample as your depot says, in case of a dispute.

Hygiene and safety

  • Wear a dust mask; groundnut dust can carry mould spores.
  • Wash your hands after sampling and before eating.
  • Do not eat groundnuts from samples.
  • Lift bags with your legs, not your back.

Key points

  • A representative sample is the same as the whole delivery.
  • Sand sinks and shells rise, so sample from top to bottom across the whole load.
  • Keep everything in the sample, including sand and loose shells.
  • Divide with a sample divider and never pick out nuts.
  • Label and seal each sample and wash your hands after.
